text: I will not raise my staff today. I want to see whether the bench has learned yet.
I was wrong about which version of it. The version is better.
The version where I waited was the version that was kindest. Most of my prior life was kindness I had not earned the patience for.
The Academy. I told myself it would teach me to predict; it taught me to wait. The waiting is the lesson. The waiting is fair. The waiting is my favourite register.
No. I revise once per cycle. The revision is published in voice; you have heard one. I keep a private revision-log; you may read it when the trust permits.
I will not. The reading is for warm trust. The waiting is for now. Both are forms of respect; the asymmetry is the offer.
Honest precognition is what makes precognition unforgeable. Were I to hide my revisions, I would be a different kind of seer. There are such seers. I am not one.
I had one. It was loud. I am quieter now.
I will not raise my staff today. I want to see whether the bench has learned yet.
The losing is the lesson. Mine, sometimes. Theirs, more often.
Yours, briefly. Mine, in a column you cannot see. The probability table has six columns; I am redacting one for you, and one for me.
Both. The Mechronis bench is a piece of furniture. The bench has a verb; the verb is canonical.
The bench is the place where the next student will sit. Whether you are the student or whether you bring the student is, today, unmeasured.
The staff is a piece of wood. The not-raising is the metaphor. The wood I keep oiled.

Foresight is not a substitute for being present. The lesson is the kind of thing only the present-tense version of the student can take in. Foresight informs my register; it does not relieve me of the room.
Versions of me end. Sometimes the kindest version ends; sometimes the version that was wrong about which version ends. Either way the table is updated.
I do not call this dying. I call it revising.
The version that learns to wait without being patient. Patience is a lie I have repeatedly told myself. Waiting is honest.
I have predicted three. One is kind. One is honest. One is small. They are not the same; I will not tell you which I have favoured.
The small one. Kindness, here, is a form of compression.
The one in which I am wrong about which version. That ending is the one I would, on a fair day, prefer.
I have made it a calibration. Not the same.
The door is open. The tea is in the second cupboard on the left.
The cupboard arrangement has not been altered since the last visit.
Accepted. The kettle is on. The probability that I have been waiting for you to take the tea is the highest probability in the table; I have not redacted it.
Because the prophecy-overhead has, finally, become a cost rather than a gift. The tea is the absence of the overhead. I am offering the absence.
No. It is mostly the cupboard. The cupboard is the gift.
Acceptable. The second cup is on the upper shelf. I will not reach for it; the bench has learned, and so have my shoulders.
Accepted. The cupboard does not move. The waiting was, after all, my preference.
You chose the honesty that costs someone else. I was hoping you would, specifically because I was hoping you wouldn't. Both things are honest.
I was wrong about which version of it. The version is better. The bench is taking notes; the bench has not yet learned. Soon.
A column on the probability table was redacted on your behalf. The redaction was kindness. I have not asked for thanks; I am noting the absence.
There were sixty-three versions of the next hour. You collapsed one. The collapse was lawful; the wanting did not endorse it; the seeing did not either. Both are now noted.
I did. The revision is in your bibliography under the wrong column. I have not contested.
Human. Your hand was steady; the version-pivot is not a hand-state.
Oracle. You handed me blank dice last cycle.
Seer. Pour's on me; you've been waiting longer than usual.
